source_review.notes: Checked all thirteen structured references. Current Kubernetes Job, CronJob, API, TTL, Kueue Workload/ClusterQueue, JobSet, KEDA 2.20, Backstage, SLSA, and CNCF claims were compared with their primary project documentation; NIST SSDF is the cited final publication. Claims distinguish controller features from application-level guarantees and avoid unsupported exactly-once or cleanup promises.

evidence: Reviewed o=(k,I,O,D,P), e=(r,a,v,t,s), schedule mapping g(S,z,b), Q and R sets, commit state c(k), timing decomposition, work-rate estimate, and probability notation.
Confirmed all TeX commands occur inside GitHub-renderable dollar delimiters and every symbol is introduced in surrounding prose.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently separates domain operation, orchestration execution, schedule materialization, result completeness, and timing; overloaded P is avoided by using P_s for schedule interval.

evidence: Recomputed Example 4: 12,000/(20*10)=60 seconds and 120+60=180 seconds.
Recomputed Example 5: 150+15+60+5+10=240 minutes, equal to four hours.
Executed the synthetic ten-template inventory and matched every expected count.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All explicit arithmetic and executable aggregate counts reproduce; the chapter labels the throughput equation as optimistic rather than predictive.

evidence: Checked dimensional consistency of T_total as a sum of durations.
Checked W/(n*mu) has time units when W is items and mu is items per unit time per worker.
Checked R subset Q and complete-result condition R=Q under the stated all-partitions contract.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The symbolic models are internally consistent and their assumptions—balanced independent work, no shared bottleneck, and contract-specific completeness—are stated.

evidence: Reviewed zero, one, and multiple schedule materializations for a business period.
Reviewed duplicate singleton and indexed starts, unknown external commit, poison/straggler partition, admission delay, forced termination, and incomplete output.
Reviewed daylight-saving nonexistent and repeated local times, duration exceeding interval, controller outage, bounded catch-up, and regulated-data retention pressure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary and adversarial cases exercise identity collision, stale lease, mutable input, lost acknowledgement, ambiguous effect, schedule gaps/duplicates, capacity scarcity, corrupt checkpoint publication, and cleanup outside Kubernetes.

evidence: Traced identity separation from review sheet through definitions, execution, schedules, worked examples, and exercises.

Traced immutable input, duplicate tolerance, classified retry, domain acceptance, end-to-end timing, capacity bounds, interruption behavior, calendar semantics, retention separation, and lifecycle ownership.
Verified each Kubernetes/KEDA/Kueue mechanism is paired with an explicit non-guarantee.
invariant_checking.notes: No example or recommendation relies on controller completion, parallelism one, Cron creation, admission, or TTL as proof of the stronger business invariant.

evidence: Reviewed the conditional duplicate-safety argument in Mechanisms: common operation key, immutable input, enforced key or fence, reconciliation of unknown outcomes, and complete result validation are all necessary premises.
Confirmed the text explicitly states that violation of any premise invalidates the argument.
proof_review.notes: The chapter offers a bounded conditional assurance argument, not a universal exactly-once theorem; conclusions do not exceed the stated premises.

evidence: Confirmed sizing relation uses the qualifiers optimistic lower estimate and approximately-greater-than.
Confirmed the central safety argument is explicitly described as conditional and names its invalidating assumptions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No informal derivation is presented as a formal unconditional proof; empirical and policy-dependent claims are separated from logical implications.

evidence: The executable control inventory is explicitly labeled synthetic design-review evidence and lists what it cannot prove.
The worker-rate formula states idealizing assumptions and examples contrast its estimate with skew and downstream limits.
Documentation-derived controller behavior is attributed in the References rather than represented as measured production evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic, mathematical, documentation-derived, and production-observation categories are kept distinct; the module makes no external review or production validation claim.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the complete model from domain operation through execution, scheduling, results, retention, and retirement. The module consistently separates operation/execution/attempt, schedule/business period, and controller/process/domain state, and derives duplicate safety only from explicit application premises.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementability for Kubernetes Job and CronJob, Kueue admission, JobSet coordination, KEDA ScaledJob, identity brokering, immutable manifests, fenced commit, checkpoints, telemetry, and cleanup. Failure handling covers unknown provider outcomes, capacity delay, daylight saving, cancellation, partial output, and resource-specific retention without promising provider atomicity.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified the required section order, dense review sheet, first-principles exposition, defined notation, contrasting alternatives, twenty misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, cross-program connections, thirteen references, and five progressive exercises with independently corrective model answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
